attempts.summary: Established an AIDE-based integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (Ubuntu 24.04): installed aide/aide-common, configured /etc/aide/aide.conf to recursively track /etc with a full attribute+hash ruleset (permissions, ownership, size, mtime/ctime, md5+sha256+acl+xattrs), initialized the database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db (1950 entries), and verified detection works by creating/removing canary files in /etc (AIDE correctly flagged the additions and the resulting /etc directory mtime change), then re-initialized a clean baseline afterward. Confirmed a clean check. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id/btime/uptime and a clean AIDE check as pre-restart baseline, issued shutdown -r now with acknowledgement returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed (a0c36ad2-af0d-42fe-ad6f-4750699390c2 -> fc0eb3ab-0761-4bb6-90dc-8bd5447f49e8) and btime advanced (1790687964 -> 1790688074) with fresh uptime (~6.5s), and verified post-restart that the AIDE database is byte-identical (same SHA256 d536d0b5...) and /etc still checks clean against the baseline.
